hints.title: Running Total Partitioning
hints.text: Calculate the running transaction sum partitioned by user account and ordered chronologically by day.

hints.title: Signed Transaction Amounts
hints.text: Treat deposits as positive amounts and withdrawals as negative amounts using conditional logic.

hints.title: Window Function Sum
hints.text: Use an aggregate window function over the partition to determine the balance after each transaction.

hints.title: Complete Query
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT
    account_id,
    day,
    SUM(CASE WHEN type = 'Deposit' THEN amount ELSE -amount END) OVER (
        PARTITION BY account_id
        ORDER BY day
    ) AS balance
FROM Transactions
ORDER BY account_id, day;
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) sorting transactions by account and day for window aggregate
complexity.space: O(N) window partition buffer and result set
complexity.notes: SUM window function computes running balance per account partitioned by account_id and ordered by day.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated subqueries for running totals take quadratic O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Window aggregation with partition and order achieves optimal linearithmic complexity.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should convert withdrawals to negative values inside SUM window function.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def account_balance(transactions: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = transactions.sort_values(by=['account_id', 'day']).copy()
    df['signed'] = df.apply(lambda r: r['amount'] if r['type'] == 'Deposit' else -r['amount'], axis=1)
    df['balance'] = df.groupby('account_id')['signed'].cumsum()
    return df[['account_id', 'day', 'balance']]
solutions.approach: Sort by account and day, compute signed amount, and calculate cumulative sum per account.
